MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 24, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ at 7:00 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Mayor Pro Tem Schmitz led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Mitchell

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-G AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 24, 2019
 B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 10, 2019

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS SEPTEMBER 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61932 THROUGH 61988 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $315,981.61; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090319 THROUGH 090619 IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $98,651.05 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $414,632.66
  WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT – AUGUST 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT – AUGUST 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 16, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

Recognizing that it was not yet 7:30 pm, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ took the following agenda
items out of order.

NEW BUSINESS (TAKEN OUT OR ORDER)

A.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION – CITY HALL RENOVATION PROJECT BY PUB
  CONSTRUCTION, INC.

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Accept the City Hall Renovation Project as
  complete; 2) Authorize the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion for the project with the
  Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder’s Office on September 25, 2019; and 3) If not
  claims are filed within 35 days after recordation; direct staff to release the 5% construction
  retention payment to PUB Construction, Inc. in the amount of $20,347.08.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 24, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired as the statutory requirement for holding the
  retention payment. City Attorney Davis noted that he would verify the statutory
  requirement prior to releasing the retention payment.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that staff was actively involved in
  ensuring a good outcome for the project and thanked staff for their efforts.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ expressed appreciation to staff for their flexibility and
  accessibility during the course of the project and for effective project management.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER
  ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ACCEPT THE CITY HALL RENOVATION PROJECT
  AS COMPLETE; AUTHORIZE THE CITY CLERK TO FILE A NOTICE OF
  COMPLETION FOR THE PROJECT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  REGISTRAR-RECORDER’S OFFICE; DIRECT STAFF TO VERIFY THE
  STATUTORY REQUIREMENTS FOR HOLDING THE RETENTION; AND
  RELEASE THE 5% CONSTRUCTION RETENTION PAYMENT TO PUB
  CONSTRUCTION, INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $20,347.08 IF NO CLAIMS ARE
  FILED WITHIN THE STATUTORY TIMEFRAME.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM:  PARADE MANAGEMENT
  AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into the attached agreement with
  Pageantry Parades to provide parade management services for the Peninsula Holiday
  Parade of Lights on December 7, 2019 in the amount of $11,250.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the announcer for this year’s parade,
  Assistant City Manager Davis stated that she would confirm who will be the announcer
  and coordinate with the Parade Subcommittee.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the cancellation policy
  referenced in Exhibit B, City Attorney Davis commented that there would be cost to the
  city if the event is cancelled, but there is no obligation to reschedule when unforeseen
  circumstances do not allow for rescheduling.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 24, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE AGREEMENT WITH PAGEANTRY
  PARADES TO PROVIDE PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE
  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 7, 2019 IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $11,250.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

C.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE LOCAL APPOINTMENT LIST AND APPOINTMENT
  PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the Commission/Committee
  appointment process for expiring terms, provide direction to staff as desired and receive
  and file this report.

  City Clerk Luce provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested adding a column that lists when the terms began
  rather than just the last appointment date.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested holding off on recruitment until letters of
  interest are received from the existing Commission/Committee Members. City Clerk Luce
  clarified that the recruitment process will not begin until after the interest among the
  current Commission/Committee members is received but there is a Government Code
  requirement that the notice of terms expiring in the calendar year be posted.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE LOCAL APPOINTMENT
  LIST AND APPOINTMENT PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS.

  There being objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ so ordered.

OLD BUSINESS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

NONE.

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

City Attorney Davis reminded Council about the dinner his office is hosting on October 16 during
the League of California Cities Conference.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 24, 2019
 CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER):

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the Equestrian Committee met to recap and discuss the
equestrian events that were held at this weekend’s City Celebration. She also thanked staff for
their efforts in organizing a successful event.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the Neighborhood Watch Leadership Group met to
discuss emergency preparedness, noting that Sgt. Tina McCoy attended the meeting. She
reminded those watching and present of the following upcoming events: October 2 – Coffee with
a Cop; October 5 - CERT Training; October 27 – Prepared Peninsula Expo; and Amateur Radio
training in November.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the Holiday Parade Committee met and is looking for
suggestions for Grand Marshal. She noted that this year’s parade will be held on Saturday,
December 7.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that there be more shade provided in the eating
area at next year’s City Celebration.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ noted that she recently attended the Los Angeles County West
Vector Control board meeting where it was reported that cases of West Nile Virus are down but
Aedes mosquito reports are on the rise and still of great concern. She reminded residents to
eliminate all standing water.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that the Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) is still reviewing and discussing the Regional Housing Needs Assessment
(RHNA) allocation numbers and proposed methodology and that he will keep the COUNCIL
apprised of any updates.

In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding an update from Cal Water, City
Manager Grammer noted that Cal Water is typically scheduled to provide a report to COUNCIL
once a month but staff continues to meet with Cal Water weekly.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that Cal Water attended the Equestrian Committee meeting and
reported that in the coming weeks, there are some bridle trails that will be impacted but equestrians
will not likely be prevented from accessing them. She added that all affected trails will be posted
and listed on the Cal Water web site.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that the COUNCIL was invited to speak at the Palos
Verdes Parent Teachers Association’s Capitol Comes to Campus Event on October 17. It was
noted that because the date conflicts with the League Conference no Council Members are
available to attend.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER):

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 24, 2019
 A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND USC PRICE EXECUTIVE EDUCATION FORUM FOR
  LOCAL LEADERS

  City Manager Grammer stated that this item was placed on the agenda to see if any Council
  Members are interested in attending the Executive Education Forum on October 25-26.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN provided a brief overview of this educational opportunity
  for Mayors and Council Members noting that over 300 leaders have attended the program.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the fee, COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN stated that the fee is a cost recovery fee, and in some instances, USC is able
  to find scholarships to help cover the cost.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ expressed her interest in attending the forum and expressed
  her appreciation to the City for supporting learning opportunities like this.

  City Attorney Davis noted that his firm is a sponsor of the program and he has participated
  as a presenter; as an observer, he noted that this is an intimate program with high level
  participants.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE ANY INTERESTED COUNCIL
  MEMBER TO ATTEND THE USC PRICE EXECUTIVE EDUCATION FORUM
  FOR LOCAL LEADERS AT THE CITY’S EXPENSE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell
  ABSTAIN:  Zerunyan

PUBLIC HEARING (7:30 P.M.)

A.  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING: ORDINANCE NO. 727 – AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CALIFORNIA AMENDING SECTION 16.04.070 OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO REPEAL OF THE
  COUNTY SUBDIVISION CODE SECTION APPLICABLE TO DURATION OF
  APPROVALS FOR LEASE PROJECTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Take Public Testimony; 2) Discuss Ordinance
  No. 727; 3) Find that the proposed ordinance is exempt from the provisions of the
  California Environmental Quality Act, per Sections 15060(c)(2) and 15061(b)(3); and 4)
  Conduct the second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 727.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) and read
  the full title of the ordinance.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 24, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, ZUCKERMAN.

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CALL FOR PUBLIC TESTIMONY.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ called for public testimony. There were
  no members of the public present to provide public testimony.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN.

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL FIND THAT THE PROPOSED ORDINANCE IS
  EXEMPT FROM THE PROVISIONS OF THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT, PER SECTIONS 15060(C)(2) AND 15061(B)(3) AND ADOPT
  ORDINANCE NO. 727 AMENDING SECTION 16.04.070 OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO REPEAL OF THE COUNTY
  SUBDIVISION CODE SECTION APPLICABLE TO DURATION OF APPROVALS
  FOR LEASE PROJECTS.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

City Clerk Luce read Ordinance No. 727 by title only.

CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

ADJOURNMENT

At 7:36 p.m. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the next
regular City Council meeting scheduled to be held on Tuesday, October 8, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in
the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling
Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
SEPTEMBER 24, 2019
